mis_merges.label: european equities
subjects: JPM's standing tactical-long EU equities thesis with index hedges
mis_merges.why: a structural bullish call and a same-day index selloff recap are opposite-valence stories that an editor would run as separate themes, not one.

mis_merges.label: financial conditions
subjects: JPM's price-based vs. quantity-based financial-conditions-index framework (with 2022 comparison)
market/futures trading-liquidity deterioration and investor long-positioning data (UST, Nikkei, gold, bitcoin futures)
mis_merges.why: the liquidity/positioning facts are a market-plumbing story that also gets its own separate labels elsewhere in the ledger, so burying them inside 'financial conditions' would cause an editor to miss or double-count a distinct liquidity theme.

notes: Fragmentation is driven less by wording variance on a single fact and more by two patterns: (1) whole single-note research pieces (the Market Ear housing note, the Nomura vol note, the GS derivatives trade-book note) chopped into 10-22 single-card labels each; (2) the same recurring cross-bank data point (Sept Fed hike odds, AVGO earnings, US equity close levels, momentum drawdown, hedge fund leverage) re-labeled slightly differently by ingestion pass. Two mis-merges bundle a standing thesis with unrelated same-day data under one label.
